name: LAMPOST
full_name: Light A-prime Multilayer Periodic Optical SNSPD Target
summary: A proof-of-concept eV-scale dark-photon search using a multilayer dielectric structure and superconducting-nanowire single-photon detectors.
detection_principle: Dark photons coherently convert in a periodic multilayer dielectric, with the optical signal detected by extremely low-dark-count SNSPDs.

sites.name: Cryogenic optical prototype involving NIST / MIT; deployment laboratory unverified
sites.location: Cryogenic optical prototype involving NIST / MIT; deployment laboratory unverified

status.label: Published experimental record; current overall operating status unverified
status.evidence: 2021 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: New Constraints on Dark Photon Dark Matter with Superconducting Nanowire Detectors in an Optical Haloscope

collaboration.name: LAMPOST Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: No signal; kinetic mixing is constrained at approximately the 10⁻¹² level in the relevant mass interval.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
